title: Contextuality as a Diagnostic of Translation-Symmetry Breaking in Translation-Invariant 1D Hamiltonians
authors: Xiao Zeng, Kaiyan Yang, Lingxia Zhang, Zizhu Wang
abstract: Bell- and contextuality-type inequalities have become practical probes of many-body quantum correlations, often involving only few-body correlators and quantities with a direct Hamiltonian interpretation such as an energy density. Here we show that, in infinite one-dimensional translation-invariant chains, contextuality can acquire a genuinely thermodynamic meaning: within the witness families studied, the maximal quantum violation coincides with spontaneous breaking of one-site translation symmetry, producing strictly $p$-periodic ground states with $p>1$. Along natural continuous interpolations between classical-bound and quantum-optimal Hamiltonians, the classical bound marks a symmetry-breaking point where competing classical periodicities are lifted in favor of a unique quantum-selected period. At the quantum optimum, the studied families admit exact finite-size reductions: a translation-invariant contextuality witness induces a $p$-site periodic-boundary-condition inequality with identical classical and quantum bounds (hence no loss under reduction), and in several cases the resulting finite inequalities are tight. This reduction turns an infinite-chain contextuality certification into a compact, hardware-testable benchmark on a small ring, requiring only local energy measurements. We establish the mechanism analytically in representative two- and three-body witness models and corroborate it more broadly using a translation-invariant adaptation of semidefinite-program hierarchies together with variational matrix-product-state algorithms.
summary: This work establishes that contextuality serves as a quantitative diagnostic for detecting spontaneous translation-symmetry breaking in 1D quantum systems. By analyzing how the maximal violation of contextuality witnesses forces the ground state into a unique periodic structure, it connects fundamental concepts from quantum information theory to condensed matter physics principles like commensurate order.
main_problem: The paper investigates contextuality as a diagnostic tool for detecting spontaneous breaking of translation symmetry in quantum systems described by translation-invariant Hamiltonians.
main_result: Maximal quantum violation of contextuality witnesses coincides with the spontaneous breaking of one-site translation symmetry, forcing the ground state into a unique, strictly periodic structure ($p>1$).
method: The analysis uses advanced mathematical tools including Semidefinite Programming (SDP) hierarchies (NPA), Matrix Product States (MPS), and variational minimization to derive lower bounds for quantum correlations.
model_or_system: The study focuses on infinite one-dimensional translation-invariant chains governed by local Hamiltonians, analyzed using contextuality witnesses derived from energy density measurements.

important_parameters: The interpolation parameter $	heta$ controls the Hamiltonian family between classical-bound and quantum-optimal regimes; system size reduction to finite rings is also key.

figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the transition from multiple degenerate periods at the classical bound to a single quantum-selected period upon increasing contextuality violation. Finite-size scaling plots show convergence of energy densities.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the connection between contextuality, symmetry breaking, and periodicity by first establishing bounds using SDPs (NPA hierarchy), then demonstrating this via MPS/variational methods, and finally showing the physical implication through period selection upon tuning Hamiltonian parameters.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, measurable quantum correlation diagnostic—contextuality—that directly maps onto fundamental concepts in condensed matter physics like spontaneous symmetry breaking and emergent periodicity.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Schematic classical-to-quantum symmetry selection along a parameterized Hamiltonian family H(θ). We assume H(θ0) saturates the classical bound while H(θ1) reaches the maximal quantum violation. As θ is tuned from θ0 to θ1, the ground-state energy density e(θ) decreases and contextuality appears. At θ0, the classical-saturating Hamiltonian has a ground space supporting multiple distinct commensurate periods. For θ > θ0, this period degeneracy is lifted and the ground state becomes strictly pQ-periodic with pQ > 1, signaling spontaneous breaking of one-site translation symmetry.
